primary.title: Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica
primary.author: Isaac Newton
primary.rationale: Newton's seminal work laying out the laws of motion and universal gravitation. It is a foundational text in physics and mathematics.

primary.title: Opticks
primary.author: Isaac Newton
primary.rationale: A comprehensive treatise on light and color, detailing Newton's experiments and theories on optics. It includes his corpuscular theory of light.

primary.title: The Chronology of Ancient Kingdoms Amended
primary.author: Isaac Newton
primary.rationale: A posthumously published work where Newton applies his mathematical and historical methods to establish a chronology of ancient empires.

secondary.title: Isaac Newton
secondary.author: James Gleick
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded biography that explores Newton's life, work, and intellectual legacy, written by a Pulitzer Prize-winning author.

secondary.title: The Principia: Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy
secondary.author: Isaac Newton
secondary.rationale: A modern translation and scholarly analysis of Newton's Principia Mathematica, providing essential context and interpretation for understanding the work.

secondary.title: Newton's Gift: How Sir Isaac Newton Forged the World We Live In
secondary.author: James Gleick
secondary.rationale: This book focuses on Newton's influence and the lasting impact of his scientific discoveries on modern society and scientific thought.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are foundational texts by Newton. Secondary sources are recent, well-regarded scholarly biographies and analyses of his work.
